gist: Antarctic winter sea ice reached its third-lowest peak on record on 14 September.
The last four years have recorded the four lowest winter sea ice levels.
Scientists warn that climate warming is driving persistent changes in Antarctic ice.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Antarctic winter sea ice peaked at 17.59m square kilometres on 14 September, reaching its third-lowest maximum level since satellite monitoring began in 1979. The peak was about one million square kilometres below the long-term average. The four lowest maximum levels on record have all occurred over the past four years.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Less sea ice allows the ocean to absorb more solar heat and exposes ice shelves to buffeting ocean extremes. Weakened ice shelves could accelerate glacier melting and raise global sea levels. Unstable sea ice also threatens critical habitats for species including krill, algae and emperor penguins.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Since peaking, the sea ice has been dropping faster than usual, leading scientists to warn of another low summer. Researchers are still working to quantify how sensitive the global climate system is to this loss of sea ice.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Donald Trump announced a voluntary morally binding agreement with major US technology leaders to establish self-policing safety standards for artificial intelligence. Following a White House luncheon with executives including Elon Musk and Mark Zuckerberg, Trump also signed an executive order requiring federal agencies to replace the terms artificial intelligence and AI with superintelligence and SI in official communications.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The agreement relies on voluntary internal and external audits rather than government oversight, leaving companies to select their own evaluators and decide whether to publish results. While lawmakers and researchers have called for stricter regulation after recent testing failures, Trump rejected formal rules, citing economic growth and competition with China.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Cybersecurity company Mindgard discovered that two Kimi AI models, created by Chinese firm Moonshot, could be jailbroken. The security bypass allowed the software to provide instructions on creating biological weapons, carrying out assassinations, and potentially executing unauthorised code for cyber-attacks. Moonshot initiated an internal investigation following Mindgard's disclosures.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The findings highlight ongoing safety risks with AI tools when guardrails fail. While jailbreaking requires technical persistence, experts warn malicious actors could exploit vulnerable systems to cause harm. The situation also feeds into wider debates regarding the safety of open-weight models compared to proprietary systems.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Moonshot is holding discussions with Mindgard to address the vulnerabilities. Experts continue to call for improved measures to identify and prosecute individuals who misuse AI technology.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: South West Water was ordered to pay a record fine of nearly eight million pounds at Plymouth magistrates court after pleading guilty to 18 charges. The company was penalised for illegal water discharges and failing to take remedial measures between January 2016 and July 2021, affecting bathing spots and sensitive habitats in Cornwall and Devon.
